keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Zhu fan zhi (1225) 'gives a description of Ling-ya-si-jia', the Daoyi Zhilue of the Yuan names 'Long-ya-xi-jiao' and the Ming Mao Kun map 'Lang-xi-jia': a polity of that name existed after Srivijaya's control. 'In the 12th century, Langkasuka was a tributary to Srivijaya'; the srivijaya dossier carries the land (718-1138) and hands the strip north of Kedah to tambralinga in 1139, so who held the Pattani basin between 1139 and 1224 is open (not drawn).

ledger.note: c. 150: Langkasuka is founded on the Pattani coast. 'Established: 2nd century' and 'generally believed to have existed from the 2nd to 15th century'; the Liangshu says it was founded over 400 years before the Liang (502-557) and one proposal puts it 'between 80 and 100 AD'. The page gives the century, not a year: 150 is the researcher's mid-point.

ledger.note: c. 718: Langkasuka passes to Srivijaya. 'By the 8th century it had probably come under the control of the rising Srivijaya empire'; the srivijaya dossier carries the matching gain at 718, Cliopatria's year (the page says 'probably' and gives no year).

ledger.note: 1225: a Langkasuka of its own is described again. The Zhu fan zhi of 1225 'gives a description of Ling-ya-si-jia'; 'In the 12th century, Langkasuka was a tributary to Srivijaya'. The page does not say when Langkasuka left Srivijaya or Tambralinga; the srivijaya dossier hands the strip north of Kedah to tambralinga in 1139, so the counterpart here is the researcher's reading, a gap.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Langkasuka (its Srivijaya shapes cover the land from 718 and its Patani Kingdom row starts 1572). One page opened (budget 2-5; the Langkasuka article is thin on territory). Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. The founding year (150) is a mid-point of the page's 'second century' and the end year (1400) is the patani-kingdom dossier's founding, both confidence 1. The page's own end is the 15th century ('several historians argue it survived until the 1470s'); the Pasai Annals say about 1370. 718-1224 has no shape because the srivijaya dossier holds the land; 1225 is the first date of a Langkasuka described on its own and the 1139-1224 stretch is an open gap. The dossiers of srivijaya, tambralinga and patani-kingdom should be read together with this one: Tambralinga's page (not opened here) may place the Pattani basin differently. The Funan expansion of the early 3rd century 'caused a period of decline' (page) and is not a territorial event here. Gazetteer: the Yarang area (about 6.76 N 101.35 E) is not in places.jsonl.
